c.v: Fascia

runs.v: is the board running along the lower roof edge that closes the rafter-tail ends and carries the gutter system. Fascia installation and repair replaces the water-rotted board in painted wood, PVC, aluminum cladding, or fiber-cement, then remounts the gutter system.

sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Fascia Installation and Repair

runs.v: Trace the Water Source Before Replacing the Board

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing inspectors trace fascia failure to the water source — a clogged gutter, a loose gutter, or a failed slope — before replacing the board, because fascia rot starts at the moisture path, not the board.

runs.v: The inspection checks the drip-edge detail too: IRC R905.2.8.5 requires the drip edge to extend at least ¼ inch below the roof sheathing, so runoff lands in the gutter, not behind the board.
Replace the Fascia and Remount the Gutter System

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing replaces the rotted fascia and remounts the gutter system, matching the board material to the eave.

runs.v: Fascia materials include painted wood, PVC, aluminum cladding, and fiber-cement: painted wood needs a repaint cycle, PVC resists moisture, aluminum cladding wraps the board against weather, and fiber-cement resists moisture and insects, per HB Elements trade guidance. Quality materials last only when fitted with precision, cut tight to the rafter tails and primed on every face.

sections.heading: Soffit and Fascia Repair Starts With a Free Soffit Check

c.v: Soffit and fascia protect roofs from moisture damage as one system: the fascia carries the gutters, and the soffit closes the underside of the eave.

runs.v: Water that rots the fascia usually reaches the soffit next, so a reliable soffit and fascia repair checks both. Proper soffit installation enhances attic ventilation, because vented soffit panels feed outside air into the attic, and soffit and fascia prevent pest intrusion into attics; the soffit-fascia corner is the usual entry point.

Newark Quality Roofing offers free roof inspections, so ask for a free soffit check with every fascia estimate. Expert soffit and fascia work matters most on Newark's older wood-trimmed houses. Soffit and fascia also improve a home's curb appeal: a straight, freshly finished roofline can enhance the exterior and elevate its aesthetics the way new siding or windows do, and aluminum or PVC components skip the repainting.

faqs.q: How do you know if fascia needs replacing?

runs.v: Peeling or blistering paint, soft and spongy spots, surface cracks and flaking, and gutters sagging or pulling from the roofline indicate fascia that needs replacing.

faqs.q: What material lasts longest for fascia?

runs.v: Aluminum, PVC, and fiber-cement fascia resist moisture longer than painted wood, which lasts roughly 15–25 years and needs a repaint cycle.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace your roof along with the fascia?

runs.v: Replace a roof when damage exceeds 25–30% of the roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost; a fascia repair stays a trim-level job that does not by itself signal roof replacement.

faqs.q: Can you replace fascia without removing the gutters?

runs.v: Fascia replacement detaches the gutter section first, because the gutters mount to the fascia and the fascia closes the rafter-tail ends behind the gutter line.

runs.v: Fascia repair cost depends on the board length, the material, and the gutter remount, and a free written estimate sets the scope before any work begins.
